pull.title: test: speed up functional tests by removing avoidable waits
pull.body:
Reduce functional test runtime:

- set noban_tx_relay = True for tests that can benefit from it.
- wake P2PInterface.wait_until as soon as a message is delivered or the connection state changes, instead of polling every 50ms.

Tested on my x86-64 machine:

Wall time (-j=18): 110.8s to 99.1s (-11%)
Accumulated: 1715s to 1411s (-17.5%)

Tests that were most affected:

| test | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| feature_maxuploadtarget | 57.9s | 6.2s |
| wallet_conflicts | 49.2s | 7.0s |
| p2p_sendheaders | 31.1s | 6.8s |
| p2p_compactblocks | 11.1s | 1.7s |
| wallet_orphanedreward | 9.3s | 5.2s |
| wallet_importprunedfunds | 4.9s | 2.9s |

events.body:
Thanks for the reviews! 

> I think `wallet_change_address.py` would be a good addition too (goes from 9s to 1.9s on my machine).

True! Looking again, I found some others tests that can benefit from noban_tx_relay = True. There may be even more but checking for it is kinda nuanced and some tests don't benefit much.

Force-pushed 8dc80cafa2ee5932c9ff499c02d6ab8e3cf2f5ef adding self.noban_tx_relay = True in wallet_exported_watchonly.py, wallet_signer.py and wallet_change_address.py.

wallet_exported_watchonly.py 7.52s -> 2.68s
wallet_signer.py 7.98s -> 2.94s
wallet_change_address.py 11.30s -> 2.29s
lgtm, but I left a nit

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -440,6 +441,10 @@ def wait_until_helper_internal(predicate, *, timeout=60, lock=None, timeout_fact
             with lock:
                 if predicate():
                     return
+                if isinstance(lock, threading.Condition):
+                    # Wake up early when the lock owner signals a state change
+                    lock.wait(check_interval)
comments.body:
lgtm, but there could be a risk that someone sets a larger explicit interval to ensure something is only checked so often and that for the time in between "nothing" happens.

I don't think there is such a case in the codebase for a lock, but it would be good to be able to make this reviewable with `git grep`.

Can you make all `check_interval` kwargs? Possibly also `timeout`:

```diff
-    def wait_until(self, test_function, timeout=60, check_interval=0.05):
+    def wait_until(self, test_function, *, timeout=60, check_interval=0.05):
```

(edit: An alternative would be to only run this when the check_interval is the default, but up to you. This is just a nit)

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -440,6 +441,10 @@ def wait_until_helper_internal(predicate, *, timeout=60, lock=None, timeout_fact
             with lock:
                 if predicate():
                     return
+                if isinstance(lock, threading.Condition):
+                    # Wake up early when the lock owner signals a state change
+                    lock.wait(check_interval)
comments.body:
Thanks! The only caller that can reach the Condition path is `P2PInterface.wait_until`, which already takes check_interval as keyword-only, so `git grep check_interval=` already covers it. Making `TestNode.wait_until` and `BitcoinTestFramework.wait_until` keyword-only seems like a good consistency change, but it's unrelated to this PR since those never pass a lock.

Grepping check_interval=, the only tests setting an explicit interval are `p2p_ping_ibd.py` and `interface_http.py`, both relying on it for stateful checks. They go through `BitcoinTestFramework.wait_until`, so they aren't affected.

Also, my take is that `wait_until` takes a predicate, which should only describe a state, so evaluating it earlier on a notification should still be correct. Using stateful checks seems like a misuse of `wait_until` to me. So I'd prefer to leave this as is.
